nodes.name: Daily Schedule
nodes.notes: Starts the workflow on a timer — daily at 6:00. No input data; downstream nodes fetch what they need.

nodes.name: Read Recent from Notion
nodes.notes: Pulls every page from the Notion database — fine for small datasets; add a filter if the database grows large. Retries 3x with 2s backoff before giving up. On failure the item leaves via the error output instead of stopping the run. Credential: Notion integration token. notion.so/my-integrations → New integration → copy the Internal Integration Token.

nodes.name: Newest First
nodes.notes: Orders items (newest first) so limits and digests pick the most relevant records.

nodes.name: Trim to Digest Size
nodes.notes: Caps the stream at 15 items to protect downstream quotas.

nodes.name: Summarize Content (AI)
nodes.notes: Map-reduce summarization chain — handles long content without blowing the context window. On failure the item leaves via the error output instead of stopping the run.

nodes.name: OpenAI Chat Model
nodes.notes: Chat model powering the AI step (model: gpt-4o-mini). Swap providers here without rewiring. Credential: OpenAI API key. platform.openai.com → API keys → create new secret key.

nodes.name: Post Digest to Microsoft Teams
nodes.notes: Posts a chat message into a Microsoft Teams channel — same role as a Slack notify, for teams standardized on Teams. Retries 3x with 2s backoff before giving up. On failure the item leaves via the error output instead of stopping the run. Credential: Microsoft OAuth2. Azure Portal → App registrations → new app → add Microsoft Graph delegated permissions.

nodes.name: Post Digest to Slack
nodes.notes: Posts a message to Slack (#reporting) — a low-latency way for the team to see automation activity without checking a dashboard. Retries 3x with 2s backoff before giving up. Slack API → Your Apps → create an app → OAuth & Permissions. n8n's Slack OAuth2 credential walks the install for you.

nodes.name: Confirm All Sends
nodes.notes: Rejoins 2 branches into one stream (mode: append) so downstream logic runs once. Watch out: Waits for every configured input. If one branch never produces items, add 'Always Output Data' upstream so this doesn't stall.

# Build a weekly summary for dashboards

**Pattern:** Scheduled Digest · **Level:** Expert · **Trigger:** Scheduled

## Overview

Runs on a schedule, and covers dashboards work end to end across Google Sheets, Slack, Notion and Microsoft Teams.

It moves through 29 working steps plus a 3-node error rail, in this order:

1. Daily Schedule
2. Read Recent from Notion
3. Newest First
4. Trim to Digest Size
5. Summarize Content (AI)
6. OpenAI Chat Model
7. Post Digest to Microsoft Teams
8. Post Digest to Slack
9. Confirm All Sends
10. Archive Digest in Google Sheets
11. Fingerprint for Idempotency
12. Drop Already-Processed Items
13. Stamp Completion Time
14. Persist Run Metadata
15. Load Previous Snapshot
16. Compute Drift vs Snapshot
17. Enrich with Reference Data
18. Fold In Enrichment Fields
19. Offload to Post-Process Sub-workflow
20. Record Sub-workflow Result
21. Serialize Run Output (CSV)
22. Archive Row Snapshot
23. Tag Pipeline Metadata
24. Guard Non-Empty kpi
25. Cap Batch Volume
26. Stamp Processing Time
27. Summarize Run Stats
28. Append Audit Row (Google Sheets)
29. Send Summary to Microsoft Teams

Anything that throws leaves the happy path at that node and goes down the red rail — Capture Failure Context → Escalate Failure to Slack → Park in Dead-Letter Queue — so a failure is reported rather than silently lost.

## Why it exists

Doing dashboards work by hand is slow and easy to get wrong, and it stops entirely when the person who does it is away. This makes the process repeatable and monitored, with failures surfaced instead of silently lost.

## Main flow

Daily Schedule → Read Recent from Notion → Newest First → Trim to Digest Size → Summarize Content (AI) → OpenAI Chat Model → Post Digest to Microsoft Teams → Post Digest to Slack → Confirm All Sends → Archive Digest in Google Sheets → Fingerprint for Idempotency → Drop Already-Processed Items → Stamp Completion Time → Persist Run Metadata → Load Previous Snapshot → Compute Drift vs Snapshot → Enrich with Reference Data → Fold In Enrichment Fields → Offload to Post-Process Sub-workflow → Record Sub-workflow Result → Serialize Run Output (CSV) → Archive Row Snapshot → Tag Pipeline Metadata → Guard Non-Empty kpi → Cap Batch Volume → Stamp Processing Time → Summarize Run Stats → Append Audit Row (Google Sheets) → Send Summary to Microsoft Teams → Capture Failure Context → Escalate Failure to Slack → Park in Dead-Letter Queue

## Use it for

- Teams keeping Google Sheets and Slack aligned by hand for dashboards
- Dashboards work where "Read Recent from Notion" is still a manual step before Google Sheets
- Dashboards work that only reaches Google Sheets on a schedule, when someone remembers to start it

## You get

- Keeps Google Sheets and Slack in step for dashboards, without anyone re-typing a row
- Safe to re-run: records already in Google Sheets or Slack are skipped, across all 32 nodes of this dashboards build
- A failed Google Sheets or Slack call is retried rather than dropped, at any of the 32 nodes in this dashboards build
- Branches rejoin before Google Sheets, so a dashboards run reports once rather than 32 times
- Every dashboards run leaves an audit row behind, alongside Google Sheets

## Before first run
Connect credentials: API key / bearer for the target API; Google OAuth2 / service account; Microsoft OAuth2; Notion integration token; OpenAI API key; Slack OAuth2.
Follow the color key: 🟦 entry · 🟪 AI · 🟫 actions · ⬜ utilities · 🟩 outputs · 🟥 error rail.
Each node has its own doc card underneath — read those before editing.

## Try it now
Sample data is pinned on the trigger — hit **Execute Workflow** to watch it flow through every node before connecting any real credentials. Unpin the trigger (right-click → Unpin) when you're ready to go live.

## Design decisions

Summarization uses a Chain, not an Agent, because the step is fixed — there's no decision about which tool to call, just 'summarize this text.' Posting to multiple channels runs as parallel branches, not sequential sends, so a slow API on one channel never delays the message that was already ready on another.

## Practice exercises

About as deep as this pattern goes — extend it:

1. Add a third notification channel and watch the Merge node's input count update.
2. Change 'Trim to Digest Size' from 15 to 5 and see how it narrows the summary's scope.
3. Swap the Summarization Chain for a Q&A Chain to answer questions instead of just recapping.

## Credentials setup

Credentials are never included in a template file, so every node below needs its own connection before the first real run. In n8n: open the node, click the Credential dropdown, choose **Create new**.

**Notion integration token**
notion.so/my-integrations → New integration → copy the Internal Integration Token.
_Gotcha:_ Then open the database → ••• → Connections → add your integration, or every call 404s.

**OpenAI API key**
platform.openai.com → API keys → create new secret key.
_Gotcha:_ Needs billing set up; a brand-new key with no credit returns 429 immediately.

**Microsoft OAuth2**
Azure Portal → App registrations → new app → add Microsoft Graph delegated permissions.
_Gotcha:_ Graph throttles with HTTP 429 — the retry setting on this node already handles it.

**Slack OAuth2**
Slack API → Your Apps → create an app → OAuth & Permissions. n8n's Slack OAuth2 credential walks the install for you.
_Gotcha:_ Needs `chat:write`. Invite the bot to the channel or posting fails with `not_in_channel`.

**Google OAuth2 / service account**
Google Cloud Console → enable Sheets API → OAuth2 client, or a Service Account.
_Gotcha:_ Using a Service Account? Share the spreadsheet with its email address or it 404s.

**API key / bearer for the target API**
Whatever the target API issues — usually a bearer token or API key.
_Gotcha:_ Store it as a credential, never typed into the node's parameters.

Set each credential up once and it is reusable across every workflow in your instance.

## Troubleshooting

**Workflow does nothing when the trigger should fire**
Cause: It is still a draft, or the trigger is inactive.
Fix: Publish/activate the workflow. Manual test runs use a different URL than production.

**A node shows a red error triangle on import**
Cause: No credential is attached yet.
Fix: Expected on a fresh import — open the node and attach a credential (see the Credentials setup note).

**HTTP node returns 401 or 403**
Cause: Wrong or unscoped credential, or the API expects a header this request isn't sending.
Fix: Verify the key directly with curl first, then confirm the auth type matches what the API documents.

**HTTP node returns 429**
Cause: Rate limited by the provider.
Fix: Raise the wait between calls or lower the batch size. Retries already back off, but they cannot beat a hard quota.

**AI node fails with an auth or quota error**
Cause: API key missing billing, or the per-minute rate limit was hit.
Fix: Confirm the provider account has credit. For rate limits, lower concurrency or switch to a higher-quota model.

**The AI returns the wrong shape or rambles**
Cause: The prompt is under-specified for the task.
Fix: Tighten the System Message: state the role, the constraints, and the exact output format you expect.

**Execution stalls at the Merge node**
Cause: One input branch produced no items, so Merge is still waiting.
Fix: Enable 'Always Output Data' on the node feeding the empty branch.

Still stuck? n8n's **Executions** tab shows the exact node that failed and the data going into it — start there rather than guessing.

## 🛟 Error handling & retries

External calls retry **3× with 2s backoff**. Anything still failing exits through its node's error output into the red error rail → context is captured and the on-call channel is alerted. Failures are also parked in a dead-letter queue for replay. Set an n8n **Error Workflow** in settings as the final safety net.

## 🤖 AI cluster

Purple nodes form one AI unit: the root node orchestrates, sub-nodes plug in via typed ports (model / memory / tools / parser). Swap the chat model without rewiring anything else. Costs scale with tokens — keep prompts lean and cap iterations.

## 🧹 Data quality

Dedupe/diff steps make re-runs safe: the same input twice will not create duplicate records. If you change the key fields, clear n8n's dedupe memory (node → 'Clear stored keys') before the next run.

## 🛠 Customize me

Quick wins: point the data nodes at your own accounts (see 🔑 lines on each card), adjust the trigger cadence, and tune thresholds/labels to your dashboards process. Every node card explains its role — safe to extend at any marked branch.

## 🔐 Security

Credentials live in n8n's credential store and are never written into node parameters — that is why this file carries none.

**Least privilege for this build**
- Google Sheets: share the single spreadsheet with the service account rather than granting drive-wide access.
- Slack: `chat:write` is enough to post. Do not add `channels:history` unless a node here actually reads messages.
- Notion: share only the target database with the integration. An integration sees nothing you have not explicitly shared.
- Microsoft Teams: restrict the app registration to the target team; tenant-wide permission is not needed to post.

The HTTP node sends a secret: keep it in a header credential, never in the URL — query strings land in proxy and execution logs.

**Do not log**
Log the identifier and the outcome, not the whole dashboards payload. n8n stores execution data verbatim, so anything a node emits is readable by everyone with instance access.
